disclaimer: Static snapshot, not a live feed. Nigerian macro data moves; verify against the primary source before making commercial decisions.

signals.name: USD / NGN
signals.note: Broadly stable in a ₦1,350–1,380 band since the 2023–24 reforms. Official and parallel rates now near-identical — the convergence matters more than the level, because it is what makes a repatriation plan modellable.

signals.name: External reserves
signals.note: Reserve cover is the buffer behind FX stability. Watch this before you commit to a naira-denominated cost base.

signals.name: Headline inflation
signals.note: Down from 25.29% a year earlier — but part of that fall reflects the NBS 2024-base CPI rebasing rather than genuine cooling. Treat the direction as real and the magnitude as partly technical when building pricing assumptions.

signals.name: Monetary policy rate
signals.note: Money is deliberately tight. Local-currency debt is expensive — fund through equity or properly documented offshore and shareholder loans instead.

signals.name: Real GDP growth
signals.note: Year-on-year, Q1 2026. Accelerating and services-led rather than oil-led, which is the more durable pattern.

signals.name: Capital imported
signals.note: Q1 2026, up 84% year-on-year. Hot money has returned decisively.

signals.name: FDI share of inflows
signals.note: 95% of Q1 2026 inflows were portfolio money. Patient capital competing for real operating assets is still thin on the ground — which, for a direct investor, is the opportunity.

signals.name: Foreign-participation capital floor
signals.note: Minimum share capital for any company with foreign participation — even 1%. The binding constraint on most foreign entrants, and the reason premature incorporation is expensive.
